rules.statement: When automation compares the files changed in a range against a protected or allow-listed path set, run `git diff --no-renames --name-only` (or `--name-status`) so a rename lists both the old and the new path.
rules.why: By default git diff can detect renames and `--name-only` then prints only the new path. Moving a protected file such as a CI workflow or manifest to an unprotected path would get past the check.
rules.check: Look for `git diff --name-only` (or `git log --name-only`) whose output is matched against protected or allowed paths and has no `--no-renames` or `--name-status`; that applies to every copy of the check.

rules.statement: Don't report that a pattern or rule has no mechanical test until you have read the test suite for it: the suite may already pin the exact string and match it against sample inputs.
rules.why: The maintainer declined such a finding because the test script already required the exact pattern in every file and matched it against positive and negative sample inputs.
rules.check: Search the repository's test scripts for the pattern or rule text and for sample inputs matched against it before you raise a missing-test finding.

rules.statement: Don't report a mismatch between the pull request description and the code when the code reflects a deliberate change requested in an earlier review round, and don't ask an automated run to edit the PR description.
rules.why: The shipped code was a tightening the maintainer asked for, and the PR description is the maintainer's to update, not the automated run's.
rules.check: Before you report a description/code mismatch, check the earlier review threads on the PR for a requested change that explains the difference.
